label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
Rohan, no sad face practice needed yet. But you're getting the uncut version, promise. And Ajay, yes, that's the post — my LinkedIn editor was busy being a cricket captain, so I'll skip the press release and just tell you.

**What actually happened**

Last Friday we let go of 6 of 14. Everyone got 2 months' pay, and we've already lined up interviews for 4 of them — two have offers, one is at a product company in HSR, one is going back to his old startup. That part I'm weirdly okay with, unfortunately.

The real problem is the bridge round from the Hyderabad fund. The term sheet was basically ready, we were doing the legal drafts, and on 28 Oct they pulled. No warning, no call, no "market turned". The partner said "we love the energy" on a call and then stopped replying for 11 days. Eleven. I have the WhatsApp where it just goes quiet — that's the industry version of a breakup text.

**Where we stand right now**

- Runway is about 5 months after the cuts. Not 5 months of panic, 5 months of working.
- App has ~41k monthly users. Plumbers and electricians side is genuinely growing — that's the part that isn't on fire.
- AC servicing bleeds money on literally every job. We're shutting that vertical down.
- New bet: housing society tie-ups. 3 societies in HSR have signed pilots already. This is where I actually think we have a real shot.

**Your money**

You and Divya put in 3 lakh in the friends round in 2025, same terms as everyone else — nothing special, nothing worse. And I want to be straight: it is at risk, but it is not gone. Nobody's written it off, and I'm not going to sit here and say "we're crushing it, relax" because that would be a lie and you'd smell it from two states away.

But I also can't promise you it's safe, because I genuinely don't know. I think the societies are a real shot, not a sure thing. If the worst happens, you'll be the first to know and I'll figure out what I owe you — I'd rather say that to you on a call with the numbers open than here in a group chat.

Can we do a call this week — you, Divya, me? I'll share the actuals: bank balance, monthly burn, cap table. No sanitised deck, no "difficult decisions" energy. You trusted me with real money, you have every right to ask, and I owe you a straight answer more than I owe this group a vibe.

Also, if this thing kills me, please don't tell amma. She asked me last week if TCS is still hiring, and now I have to explain what a bridge round is to a woman who thinks "PF" is a snack.

One more thing — I eat Maggi at the office at 11pm so often that the security uncle now asks if I want masala or plain. He has opinions. He is also, unfortunately, my most consistent source of support right now.

Laying off those 6 was the worst day of my life. Worse than failing maths in 2nd sem, and I still think about that. So I get exactly why you're asking.

Saturday. I'll be there. Pranav is buying, so the plan is biryani, beer, and I will not look at my phone between 7 and 10. That's the only promise I can actually keep this week.

reasons: Never says he is fine, which the request asked for; Saturday attendance and Pranav buying are covered, and the piece's other bullet points are covered too.
It does not say that Karthik is fine.
